## What's at stake

The risks of non-compliance extend well beyond a fine. Here's what organizations in your space face.

### DOJ Enforcement & Federal Investigations

- The DOJ finalized the ADA Title II rule in April 2024
- Agencies that miss the deadline face federal compliance orders
- DOJ complaints can trigger mandatory remediation timelines
- Documented non-compliance worsens liability in any subsequent lawsuit

### Constituent Lawsuits & ADA Complaints

- Any resident can file an ADA complaint against a government entity
- Online portals, permit systems, and public records must be accessible
- Lawsuits from advocacy groups increasingly target government sites
- Settlement costs routinely exceed $25,000 — before remediation

### Reputational & Operational Risk

- Inaccessible websites exclude constituents with disabilities
- Negative press coverage from accessibility complaints is common
- Staff time spent on manual accommodation requests is significant
- Procurement rules increasingly require accessible digital services

### How ADA Compliant Helps Government Teams

- Scan any page in 30 seconds — no IT involvement needed
- Every issue comes with suggested fix code for your developers
- Timestamped Compliance Audit Log shows good-faith effort
- Automated weekly monitoring catches regressions before the deadline

Does ADA Title II apply to my agency's website?

Yes. The 2024 DOJ final rule under ADA Title II applies to all state and local government entities — including cities, counties, school districts, transit agencies, courts, and special districts. Websites and mobile apps must meet WCAG 2.2 AA by April 24, 2026 (for entities with 50,000+ population) or April 26, 2027 (for smaller entities).

What happens if we miss the April 2026 deadline?

Agencies that fail to comply face DOJ enforcement actions, constituent ADA complaints, and potential federal lawsuits. There is no grace period after the deadline — non-compliance can be raised in any legal action immediately.

Can automated scanning replace a full accessibility audit?

Automated tools like ADA Compliant can quickly identify a significant portion of WCAG 2.2 AA issues. However, comprehensive compliance typically also requires manual testing with assistive technologies. Our scans are a strong starting point and are particularly valuable for identifying and fixing the most common, high-risk violations quickly.

How does the Compliance Audit Log help our legal defense?

The timestamped Audit Log in our Pro plan documents every scan, every issue found, and when it was remediated. This creates a paper trail demonstrating your agency's good-faith compliance effort — which is recognized in ADA enforcement as a mitigating factor.
